chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Ali ibn Khalid al-Aquli, from Karram, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed li'an with his wife and disowned her child, then contradicted himself after the li'an, claiming that the child was his: Is it returned to him? He said: 'Yes, it is returned to him, and he does not leave his child who has no inheritance for him. As for the woman, she is not permissible (to him) forever.'

I asked him: Who inherits the child? He said: 'His maternal uncles.' I said: 'What if his mother died, and the boy inherited her, then the boy died? Who inherits him?' He said: 'The agnates of his mother.' I said to him: 'So he inherits his maternal uncles?' He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and marital status rulings for a child and wife after li'an if the father later claims the child?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the legal status of a child from li'an is clarified: although paternity is restored to the father, the child does not inherit from him, and the wife remains permanently forbidden. The hadith further details the inheritance chain, specifying that maternal uncles inherit the child, and if the mother dies, her agnatic relatives inherit the child, illustrating the distinct Shia jurisprudence regarding the 'son of li'an'.
